title: General Surgery Diploma — The Pelvis & Perineum MCQ Bank (96 Questions)

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: At which vertebral level does the sigmoid colon typically end and become the rectum?
questions.explanation: The sigmoid colon begins at the pelvic brim as a continuation of the descending colon and ends at the middle piece of the sacrum (S3) where it becomes the rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the shape of the root of the sigmoid mesocolon attached to the posterior pelvic wall?
questions.explanation: The root of the sigmoid mesocolon has an inverted V-shape, with its left limb along the external iliac artery and right limb extending to the 3rd piece of the sacrum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the approximate length of the human rectum?
questions.explanation: The rectum measures approximately 5 inches (13 cm) in length, following the curve of the sacrum and coccyx.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The transverse folds of the rectum (Houston’s valves) are permanent folds formed by mucous membrane and which muscular layer?
questions.explanation: Houston’s valves are formed by the mucous membrane folding along with the inner circular muscle layer (two on the left, one on the right).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Regarding the peritoneal covering of the rectum, which statement is completely accurate?
options: Upper 1/3 covered on front and sides; middle 1/3 on front only; lower 1/3 is uncovered
Entire rectum is covered by peritoneum
Only the lower third has a peritoneal coat
questions.explanation: Peritoneum covers the upper third on front and sides, middle third on the front only, and leaves the lower third completely bare.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which artery provides the main blood supply to the upper third of the rectum?
options: Superior rectal artery (direct continuation of IMA)
questions.explanation: The superior rectal artery is the direct continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery supplying the upper rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Venous blood from the superior rectal vein drains ultimately into which system?
options: Inferior vena cava via internal iliac veins
Portal venous system via inferior mesenteric and splenic veins
questions.explanation: Superior rectal vein drains into the inferior mesenteric vein, establishing the portal venous drainage of the upper rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the primary sensory modality perceived within the rectum and upper anal canal?
questions.explanation: The rectum and upper anal canal possess autonomic innervation (inferior hypogastric plexus) and are sensitive exclusively to stretch, not somatic pain.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In the male, what structure lies immediately anterior to the lower third of the rectum?
options: Base of the urinary bladder, seminal vesicles, and ampulla of vas deferens
questions.explanation: Anterior relations of the lower third of the rectum in males include the bladder base, seminal vesicles, and ampulla of the vas deferens.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In the female, what structure lies immediately anterior to the upper two-thirds of the rectum?
options: Sigmoid colon, ileum, and pouch of Douglas (rectouterine pouch)
questions.explanation: The upper two-thirds of the female rectum are separated anteriorly from coils of small bowel and sigmoid by the rectouterine pouch (Douglas’ pouch).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which ligament/fold connects the upper rectum to the sacrum posteriorly?
questions.explanation: The fascia of Waldeyer (mesorectal fascia) suspends the rectum from the sacrum and is a key surgical landmark in total mesorectal excision (TME).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The middle rectal artery is typically a branch of which major vessel?
questions.explanation: The middle rectal artery arises directly from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Lymphatic drainage from the upper rectum goes primarily to which lymph node group?
options: Pararectal and inferior mesenteric lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Upper rectal lymphatics follow the superior rectal vessels to pararectal nodes and up to the inferior mesenteric lymph node chain.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the arterial blood supply to the lower third of the rectum and anal canal?
options: Inferior rectal artery (branch of internal pudendal)
questions.explanation: The lower rectum and anal canal receive blood from the inferior rectal arteries branching from the internal pudendal arteries.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which autonomic nerves provide sympathetic input to the rectum?
questions.explanation: Sympathetic fibers originate from T11-L2 via lumbar splanchnics and the hypogastric plexuses, mediating inhibition of peristalsis and contraction of sphincters.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Parasympathetic supply to the rectum and distal colon promotes:
options: Relaxation of internal sphincter and inhibition of motility
Contraction of internal sphincter and vasoconstriction
Peristalsis and relaxation of the internal anal sphincter
questions.explanation: Pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4) provide parasympathetic motor supply to the distal gut and inhibitory input to the internal anal sphincter.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: During low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, injury to the pelvic autonomic nerves running along the pelvic sidewall results in:
questions.explanation: Preservation of pelvic splanchnic nerves and hypogastric plexuses is critical to avoid postoperative urinary retention and sexual dysfunction.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The rectosigmoid junction is clinically defined from inside by:
options: The termination of taeniae coli into a continuous outer longitudinal muscle coat
questions.explanation: At the rectosigmoid junction, the three separate taeniae coli spread out to form a continuous longitudinal muscle layer around the rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which peritoneal pouch is the lowest point of the peritoneal cavity in the erect or semi-recumbent female?
questions.explanation: The rectouterine pouch (Douglas' pouch) is the most dependent part of the female peritoneal cavity, where fluid or pelvic pathology accumulates.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which fascia separates the rectum posteriorly from the sacrum and presacral veins?
questions.explanation: Waldeyer's fascia (posterior mesorectal fascia) is the avascular plane behind the rectum that must be sharply dissected during rectal cancer surgery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the standard length of the adult surgical anal canal?
questions.explanation: The anal canal extends downward and backward from the anorectal junction to the anus, measuring about 4 cm (1.5 inches).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The pectinate (dentate) line marks the junction between:
questions.explanation: The dentate line represents the embryological transition zone between endoderm (hindgut) and ectoderm (proctodeum), creating a major landmark for innervation, venous drainage, and lymphatic spread.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics applies to the anal canal ABOVE the pectinate line?
options: Sensitive to somatic pain, touch, and temperature
Lined by stratified squamous keratinized epithelium
Lined by columnar epithelium and sensitive to stretch only
Drains into superficial inguinal lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Above the pectinate line, the anal canal is lined by columnar/transitional epithelium, supplied by visceral afferents (stretch-sensitive), and drains to internal iliac nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics applies to the anal canal BELOW the pectinate line?
options: Sensitive to somatic pain via the inferior rectal nerve
Drained by the portal venous system
questions.explanation: Below the dentate line, the anoderm is somatic-innervated by the inferior rectal nerve (pudendal branch), making it exquisitely sensitive to pain, touch, and temperature.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Internal hemorrhoids originate from vascular cushions located:
options: Below the pectinate line in the perianal skin
In the submucosa above the pectinate line (typically at 3, 7, and 11 o'clock)
questions.explanation: Internal hemorrhoids are prolapsing submucosal vascular cushions located above the pectinate line at specific clock positions (3, 7, and 11 o'clock in lithotomy position).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: External hemorrhoids are covered by:
options: Modified skin (anoderm) containing somatic pain fibers
questions.explanation: External hemorrhoids are dilatations of the inferior rectal venous plexus located below the pectinate line, covered by somatically innervated anoderm.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the functional composition of the anorectal ring palpable on digital rectal examination?
options: Puborectalis sling, deep external sphincter, and upper internal sphincter
questions.explanation: The anorectal ring is a crucial muscular ring formed by the puborectalis, deep external sphincter, and upper internal sphincter; its transection causes permanent fecal incontinence.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The internal anal sphincter is a thickening of which muscle layer of the gut wall?
options: Skeletal muscle of the pelvic floor
questions.explanation: The internal sphincter is an involuntary smooth muscle thickening formed by the inner circular layer of the rectal muscle coat.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The external anal sphincter is composed of skeletal muscle and is divided into three parts:
questions.explanation: The external sphincter is voluntary skeletal muscle divided into subcutaneous, superficial, and deep portions.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What nerve innervates the external anal sphincter?
options: Inferior rectal nerve (branch of pudendal nerve, S2-S4)
questions.explanation: Voluntary control of the external anal sphincter is provided by the inferior rectal nerve (pudendal nerve, S2-S4).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the white line of Hilton (interscaphoid line)?
options: The junction between rectum and sigmoid
The intersphincteric groove felt internally between internal and subcutaneous external sphincters
questions.explanation: Hilton’s white line marks the intersphincteric groove position inside the anal canal, separating non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium from true perianal skin.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Lymphatic drainage from the anal canal BELOW the pectinate line flows primarily into:
options: Medial group of superficial inguinal lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Because the lower anal canal is somatic/cutaneous, its lymph drains directly into the superficial inguinal lymph nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The ischiorectal (ischioanal) fossa is bounded medially by:
options: Levator ani muscle and external anal sphincter
questions.explanation: The wedge-shaped ischiorectal fossa is bounded medially by the levator ani and anal canal, and laterally by the obturator internus muscle.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Alcock’s canal (pudendal canal) is located within the lateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa and is formed by a splitting of:
questions.explanation: Alcock’s canal is a fascial tunnel within the obturator fascia on the lateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which major structures are transmitted through Alcock’s canal?
options: Internal pudendal vessels and pudendal nerve
questions.explanation: The pudendal canal transmits the internal pudendal artery and vein, and the pudendal nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the perineal body (central tendon of the perineum)?
options: A fibromuscular node anchored between the anal canal and urogenital diaphragm
questions.explanation: The perineal body is a vital fibromuscular junction where multiple perineal muscles converge, essential for pelvic floor integrity.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which muscles converge to form the perineal body?
options: Bulbospongiosus, superficial & deep transverse perinei, external anal sphincter, and levator ani
questions.explanation: The perineal body anchors the urogenital and anal triangles, receiving insertions from bulbospongiosus, transverse perinei, external sphincter, and levator ani.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Anal fissures most commonly occur at which anatomical clock position due to poor local perfusion?
questions.explanation: Over 85-90% of typical anal fissures occur in the posterior midline because of relatively sparse blood perfusion in that zone.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Denonvilliers’ fascia (rectovesical fascia) in males is located between:
questions.explanation: Denonvilliers’ fascia is the rectovesical septum separating the posterior prostate and seminal vesicles from the anterior rectal wall.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In an intersphincteric perianal abscess, pus accumulates between:
questions.explanation: Intersphincteric abscesses are located in the intersphincteric space between the internal and external anal sphincters.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the primary function of the puborectalis muscle during continence?
options: To pull the anorectal junction anteriorly, maintaining the 90-degree anorectal angle
To compress the external urethral sphincter
questions.explanation: Puborectalis acts as a dynamic muscular sling that maintains the acute anorectal flexure, crucial for resting fecal continence.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: An abscess located in the ischiorectal fossa typically causes:
options: Throbbing perianal pain aggravated by sitting, with localized swelling/erythema
questions.explanation: Ischiorectal abscesses fill the fossa with pus, producing marked systemic sepsis signs, throbbing pain, and fluctuant swelling beside the anus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Horseshoe abscesses in the perianal region spread by tracking around the rectum through which space?
questions.explanation: Infection originating in posterior crypts can track through the deep post-anal space into both ischiorectal fossae, forming a horseshoe abscess.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What lymphatic trunks drain the pelvic viscera into the systemic circulation?
options: Thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct
questions.explanation: Pelvic lymph eventually ascends via lumbar trunks into the cisterna chyli and thoracic duct.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which nerve provides somatic sensory innervation to the skin of the scrotum/labia majora and perineum?
questions.explanation: The pudendal nerve provides somatic sensation to the entire perineum, including scrotum/labia and the anal canal below the dentate line.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the maximum normal physiological capacity of the adult urinary bladder when fully distended?
questions.explanation: When fully distended, the adult bladder can hold 500 ml or more as it rises above the pubic crest into the hypogastric region.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The trigone of the urinary bladder is characterized by:
options: Presence of prominent mucosal folds (rugae) throughout
Being a smooth triangular area firmly adherent to underlying muscle, lacking rugae
Containing mucous glands and hair follicles
questions.explanation: The trigone is bounded by the two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral meatus; its mucosa is smooth and tightly bound because it lacks a submucosal layer.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which part of the urinary bladder surface is covered by peritoneum in both sexes?
questions.explanation: The superior surface of the bladder is intraperitoneal, covered by peritoneum that reflects onto the anterior abdominal wall and uterus/rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Sympathetic innervation to the urinary bladder (inhibiting detrusor, contracting sphincter) arises from:
options: T11, T12, L1, L2 spinal segments
questions.explanation: Sympathetic preganglionic fibers originate from thoracolumbar segments T11-L2 via the superior and inferior hypogastric plexuses.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Parasympathetic innervation responsible for micturition (contracting detrusor, relaxing sphincter) arises from:
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic fibers (nervi erigentes) originate from sacral segments S2-S4 to mediate bladder emptying.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The retropubic space (space of Retzius) is located between:
questions.explanation: The retropubic space of Retzius is an extraperitoneal fat-containing space between the pubic bones and the anterior bladder wall.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In males, the base of the urinary bladder is directly related posteriorly to:
options: Seminal vesicles and ampulla of ductus deferens
questions.explanation: The posterior surface (base) of the male bladder rests against the seminal vesicles and vas deferens.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The ureters enter the urinary bladder at:
options: The superolateral angles of the trigone
The anterior wall near the apex
questions.explanation: Ureters pierce the posterolateral wall of the bladder obliquely at the upper corners of the trigone, creating a valvelike antireflux mechanism.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What prevents urine reflux from the bladder back into the ureters during micturition?
options: Active sphincter muscles around ureteric orifices
Oblique intramural course of the ureter through the bladder wall muscle
High pressure in the renal pelvis
questions.explanation: The tunnel-like oblique course of the ureter through the detrusor muscle acts as a physiological one-way valve during bladder contraction.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The arterial supply to the urinary bladder is derived primarily from branches of:
options: Internal iliac artery (superior and inferior vesical arteries)
questions.explanation: Superior and inferior vesical arteries branching from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery supply the bladder.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Venous drainage from the bladder forms a plexus around the neck and base that drains into:
questions.explanation: The vesical venous plexus drains into the internal iliac veins.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Lymphatics from the urinary bladder drain into which lymph node groups?
options: External and internal iliac lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Lymphatic drainage from the bladder follows vesical vessels to internal and external iliac lymph nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The median umbilical ligament is a fibrous remnant of which embryonic structure?
questions.explanation: The urachus (embryonic allantoic stalk) obliterates to form the median umbilical ligament extending from bladder apex to umbilicus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which muscle forms the primary voluntary sphincter of the male urethra in the deep perineal pouch?
questions.explanation: The sphincter urethrae muscle surrounding the membranous urethra in the urogenital diaphragm provides voluntary urinary control.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In females, the urethra is approximately how long?
questions.explanation: The female urethra is short (about 4 cm long), passing directly from bladder to vestibule anterior to the vagina.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which part of the male urethra is surrounded by the prostate gland?
questions.explanation: The prostatic urethra traverses the prostate gland from base to apex, receiving prostatic ducts and ejaculatory ducts at the verumontanum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The most vulnerable site of iatrogenic injury to the male urethra during catheterization or instrumentation is:
options: Membranous urethra at the urogenital diaphragm
questions.explanation: The membranous urethra is fixed within the urogenital diaphragm and represents a narrow, less distensible segment prone to tearing.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In pelvic fractures with disruption of the pubic symphysis, which part of the male urethra is most frequently torn?
questions.explanation: Shear forces at the prostatomembranous junction during pelvic ring fractures commonly cause posterior urethral disruption.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The ductus deferens crosses over which major vessel as it enters the pelvis from the inguinal canal?
questions.explanation: Entering the deep ring, the vas deferens hooks around the inferior epigastric artery and crosses external iliac vessels to enter the pelvis.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The seminal vesicles are located between:
questions.explanation: Seminal vesicles lie retrovesically between the posterior bladder base and the anterior rectal wall.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which muscle forms the main bulk of the pelvic diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The pelvic floor (diaphragm) is formed primarily by the paired levator ani and coccygeus muscles.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The levator ani muscle consists of which three major subdivisions?
options: Superficial, middle, and deep external sphincters
questions.explanation: Levator ani is subdivided into puborectalis, pubococcygeus, and iliococcygeus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the primary nerve supply to the levator ani muscle?
options: Direct branches from S4 (and pudendal nerve branches)
questions.explanation: Levator ani is innervated directly by anterior primary rami of S4 and the perineal branch of the pudendal nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which pelvic muscle exits the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen?
questions.explanation: The piriformis muscle originates from the anterior sacrum and passes laterally through the greater sciatic foramen to the greater trochanter.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The obturator internus muscle exits the lesser sciatic foramen after wrapping around which bony landmark?
questions.explanation: The tendon of obturator internus turns at a right angle around the ischial spine (lesser sciatic notch) to enter the lesser sciatic foramen.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which nerve runs directly on the anterior surface of the piriformis muscle within the pelvis?
questions.explanation: The sacral plexus lies on the piriformis muscle, with the large sciatic nerve emerging directly anterior to it.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the landmark used during pudendal nerve block in obstetrics or perineal surgery?
questions.explanation: The pudendal nerve crosses the sacrospinous ligament near its attachment to the ischial spine, making the ischial spine the target landmark for infiltration.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The obturator nerve enters the medial thigh through the obturator canal accompanied by:
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve and vessels pass through the obturator canal in the superior pubic ramus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In radical hysterectomy or low pelvic surgery, which ureteric relation is a frequent site of iatrogenic ligation?
options: As it crosses the pelvic brim
Where it is crossed anteriorly by the uterine artery ('water under the bridge')
Where it enters the bladder trigone
As it runs behind the renal vessels
questions.explanation: The ureter passes under the uterine artery near the lateral fornix of the vagina ('water under the bridge'), placing it at high risk during ligation of uterine vessels.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which lymph nodes represent the primary sentinel station for lymphatic spread of cervical, vaginal, and distal rectal cancers?
options: Internal iliac and obturator lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Internal iliac and obturator lymph nodes receive primary drainage from deep pelvic viscera and genitalia.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Pelvic fascia is condensed in certain regions to form important surgical ligaments, such as the cardinal (transverse cervical) ligament, which transmits:
options: Uterine vessels and autonomic plexuses to the uterus/cervix
questions.explanation: The cardinal ligaments extend from the lateral pelvic walls to the cervix/upper vagina, transmitting the uterine vessels.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the main support of the uterus preventing prolapse?
options: Levator ani muscle (pelvic diaphragm) and cardinal-uterosacral ligament complex
questions.explanation: Apical support (cardinal/uterosacral complex) and level diaphragm support (levator ani) cooperate to maintain uterine position.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: During a low anterior resection, total mesorectal excision (TME) is performed within which anatomical plane to minimize local recurrence and nerve injury?
options: Avascular presacral space outside the mesorectal fascia (visceral fascia of rectum)
questions.explanation: Dissection in the 'holy plane' between the parietal pelvic fascia and visceral mesorectal fascia protects pelvic autonomic nerves and removes regional lymph nodes intact.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What structure marks the boundary between the greater (false) pelvis and lesser (true) pelvis?
options: Pelvic brim (pectineal line, arcuate line, sacral promontory)
questions.explanation: The pelvic brim (linea terminalis) forms the circular inlet dividing the abdominal false pelvis from the true pelvic cavity.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In cases of pelvic fracture with massive retroperitoneal bleeding, the primary source of arterial hemorrhage is typically branches of:
options: Internal iliac artery (e.g., internal pudendal, superior gluteal)
questions.explanation: The posterior and anterior divisions of the internal iliac artery supply the pelvic walls and viscera and are the primary source of life-threatening bleeding in unstable pelvic ring fractures.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which structures are contained in the anal triangle of the perineum?
options: The anal canal and ischiorectal fossae
The urethra and external genitalia only
questions.explanation: The anal triangle contains the anal canal and the ischiorectal fossae.
questions.source: The Pelvis & Perineum — Slides.pdf
questions.reference_snapshot: The slide states that the anal triangle contains the anal canal and ischiorectal fossae. PDF p. 14; slide 151

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which structure is listed as an anterior relation of the anal canal?
questions.explanation: The perineal body and urogenital diaphragm are the stated anterior relations of the anal canal.
questions.source: The Pelvis & Perineum — Slides.pdf
questions.reference_snapshot: The relations list names the perineal body and urogenital diaphragm anteriorly. PDF p. 15; slide 152

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What is the posterior relation of the anal canal?
questions.explanation: The slide identifies the anococcygeal body as the posterior relation.
questions.source: The Pelvis & Perineum — Slides.pdf
questions.reference_snapshot: The relations list gives the anococcygeal body posteriorly. PDF p. 15; slide 152

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: In which direction does the anal canal pass from the anorectal junction toward the anus?
questions.explanation: The anal canal passes downward and backward from the anorectal junction.
questions.source: The Pelvis & Perineum — Slides.pdf
questions.reference_snapshot: The slide describes the canal as passing downward and backward. PDF p. 15; slide 152

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which nerve supply is specified for the external anal sphincter?
options: Inferior rectal nerve and perineal branch of S4
questions.explanation: The external sphincter receives the inferior rectal nerve (from the pudendal nerve) and the perineal branch of S4.
questions.source: The Pelvis & Perineum — Slides.pdf

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Where does the outer longitudinal smooth-muscle layer of the anal canal descend?
options: Between the internal and external anal sphincters
Between the two layers of the bladder wall

questions.reference_snapshot: The slide describes this layer as descending between the internal and external sphincters. PDF p. 19; slide 156

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which epithelial lining characterizes the lower half of the anal canal in the lecture slides?

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which artery supplies the lower half of the anal canal according to the slides?
questions.explanation: The lower half is supplied by the inferior rectal artery, a branch of the internal pudendal artery.
questions.source: The Pelvis & Perineum — Slides.pdf
questions.reference_snapshot: The lower-half arterial supply entry names the inferior rectal artery from the internal pudendal artery. PDF p. 22; slide 159

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: The inferior rectal vein drains first into which vein, as described in the slides?
questions.explanation: The inferior rectal vein drains into the internal pudendal vein before reaching the internal iliac vein and systemic circulation.
questions.source: The Pelvis & Perineum — Slides.pdf
questions.reference_snapshot: The lower-half venous drainage pathway begins with the inferior rectal vein entering the internal pudendal vein. PDF p. 22; slide 159

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which lymph nodes receive lymph from the upper half of the anal canal in the slide table?
options: Superior rectal nodes, then pararectal and inferior mesenteric nodes
Deep inguinal nodes, then external iliac nodes

questions.source: The Pelvis & Perineum — Slides.pdf

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What configuration do the puborectalis fibres form around the anorectal junction?
options: A complete circular ring around the anal verge
A straight band between the ischial tuberosities
A V-shaped ligament behind the coccyx

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which structures form the lateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa?
options: Obturator internus, obturator fascia, and pudendal canal

questions.reference_snapshot: The boundary list names the superficial and deep transverse perineal muscles anteriorly. PDF p. 25; slide 162

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: Which named nerve and vessels are contents of the ischiorectal fossa?
questions.explanation: The fossa contains the inferior rectal nerve and vessels; the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels lie within the pudendal canal.

questions.reference_snapshot: The contents list includes inferior rectal nerve and vessels, followed by pudendal structures within the canal. PDF p. 26; slide 163

questions.subject: PELV
questions.stem: What forms the pudendal canal?
options: A splitting of the obturator fascia
A tunnel through the sacrotuberous ligament
A passage through the levator ani
A division of the perineal membrane

Lower half of the anal canal and perianal skin only
Levator ani and skin over the sacrum
